findings.title: Workflow result publication constructs its verification authority from metadata without verifying retained content
findings.evidence: WorkflowEngine::persist reads the successful attempt's evidence artifact string, loads the Session's unit, and directly constructs WorkflowPublication { authority, artifact }. It never runs ResultStore::verify or consumes a private result of equivalent graph/manifest verification. publish_workflow_result_tx then checks only database Ready metadata and matching revision/dependency strings before making the artifact Published and closing finalization in the same Task/Workflow/Context transaction. This bypasses the existing standalone ResultStore::publish producer, which explicitly verifies the retained manifest, private refs and full graph before its Store publication. The new descriptor's comment says it is produced after retained graph verification, but its actual new producer does not establish that condition. A Ready artifact whose manifest/ref/object has disappeared or become corrupt after capture is still promoted by this new path if the metadata remains matching. The new atomic workflow test intentionally uses nonexistent /tmp fixture repository/manifest paths and succeeds, so it proves ledger atomicity only and does not supply the missing content proof.
findings.contract: Approved R2 requires retained exact content and correct immutable review/test inputs; approved design section 5 publication checks retained content identity and stops affected advancement on missing/corrupt retained content. The already-existing ResultStore::publish illustrates the explicit verification boundary. This is a defect in the newly added publication consumer, not a finding solely for future unconnected preparation/Registry integration.
findings.impact: Task revision, passed Workflow phase evidence and immutable ContextVersion can advance to a Published artifact with no usable retained graph. Transactional consistency among database rows does not establish actual retained-SHA correctness.
findings.fix_direction: Require a nonserializable verification result produced outside the Store mutex by the real retained-result verification path, binding exact artifact/unit/scope/version/manifest and authority, then CAS it with current artifact metadata in the coordinated transaction. Do not construct that result from evidence strings/Ready labels. Keep the existing raw-helper migration limitation explicit; refuse this publication path if its required verifier is not yet safely available. Keep file/Git verification outside held SQL/SharedStore locks.
minimal_causal_controls: Capture a genuine Ready retained artifact with existing ResultStore, bind a managed successful phase, then remove/corrupt its manifest or retained ref/object before workflow completion. Completion must refuse with artifact still Ready/Invalid as appropriate and unchanged Task revision/context pointer/passed phase; an intact control must atomically publish all rows.
Alter a verification-bound artifact/version between out-of-lock verification and the publication transaction and require CAS refusal.

Compiled omission of actual content verification must admit the missing/corrupt retained artifact and fail the negative consumer assertion. Keep ledger-only fixtures explicitly separate from graph qualification.

findings.title: Explicit executor retirement makes open readonly predecessors fail the next fresh-generation reservation
findings.evidence: reserve_execution now requires every open readonly predecessor's generation to equal the current task_execution prior generation before it can retire those predecessors. But retire_execution_as increments task_execution generation when retiring an Executor and closes/releases only that Executor. Open Reviewer/Verifier units of the preceding generation remain open. A legitimate state with a current Executor and readonly unit reviewing an older retained artifact is supported by the new control's final concurrent-admission case. Retiring that Executor with cancel_task=false changes task_execution from g to g+1; the readonly unit remains g. The next fresh Executor reservation then fails the new Some(previous.generation) == prior check. The readonly unit's ordinary retire operation also fails validate_authority because its generation is already fenced. Without a restart or separately implemented recovery it stays open and charged even though no live Executor prevents a fresh attempt. The added replacement test reserves a fresh Executor directly after publication and does not cover the existing explicit-retirement path.
findings.contract: R3 allows retry after fencing in a new namespace, retains exact generation identity, and keeps cleanup separate; R5 requires cancelled/retired capacity to retire fairly. The selected new predecessor-close behavior should compose with the existing NativeSessions::cancel / AttemptManager::retire path. No relaxation of younger/foreign unit authority is needed.
findings.impact: A normal retire/fresh-retry flow can be stranded by its own already-fenced readonly units, retaining their quota leases and preventing independent fresh local work.
findings.fix_direction: Either close/release the Task's applicable readonly units atomically when executor retirement advances their generation, or allow the new reservation to conservatively retire authentic older already-fenced readonly predecessors while rejecting foreign/younger/contradictory identities. Preserve their known work and artifacts, never reopen their native authority.
minimal_causal_controls: Publish a real or explicitly ledger-only prior artifact, admit a current Executor and readonly Reviewer/Verifier for that Task/current generation, acquire the readonly quota lease, then call the existing Executor retire(cancel_task=false) operation and reserve a fresh Executor. Require successful fresh unique names and closure/release of old readonly flags/waiters/leases, with immutable artifact and known work preserved.
Include the current-generation direct replacement positive, an already retired predecessor, a live Executor negative, and foreign/younger predecessor negatives.
Compiled restoration of the exact-equality-only check or omission of readonly closure on the selected fix path must make this explicit-retire/fresh-retry consumer fail.

findings.title: Executor stop still advances generation without retiring same-generation readonly units, stranding capacity and refusing the next attempt
findings.evidence: The new reservation path retires readonly predecessor flags and leases atomically before admitting a new executor. However the actual private NativeAdapter stop vtable calls NativeSessions::cancel, which calls retire_execution(..., false). retire_execution_as closes only the selected executor unit and advances task_execution.generation at execution.rs:773; it releases only that selected unit's quota at 782 and does not retire open reviewer/verifier siblings. validate_authority still applies the current Task-generation predicate to every kind. Their supervisor finish/fallback retirement consequently fail the stale-generation predicate; the still-open unit also prevents Session closure. On a later new executor reservation, the added predecessor guard requires previous.generation == prior (execution.rs:539), so this previously allowed readonly unit now causes reservation to fail before it can be closed.
causal_sequence: Publish an executor artifact A, fully closing its executor permissions, then reserve/start a fresh executor E in generation g.

While E is active, admit reviewer R or verifier V from published A. This is allowed by prepare_snapshot/reserve_execution: the artifact is immutable and published, R/V inherit generation g, and the executor-only uniqueness index does not exclude them.

Call the actual NativeAdapter::stop for E. NativeSessions::cancel retires E with cancel_task=false, advancing the Task generation to g+1 while leaving R/V's native_effects_open/result_finalization_open flags and quota leases unchanged.

R/V's authority fence fails; Core terminal persistence and fallback retire_execution cannot close an old generation. The lease remains active and Session closure fails because native_effects_open is still true.

AttemptManager::prepare for the next executor encounters the new predecessor identity guard: the open readonly predecessor has generation g, whereas prior is g+1. Reservation rolls back instead of closing it. The Task retry is blocked, and stranded leases also consume sibling provider/global capacity.
findings.impact: The main round6 revised H2 is fixed only for generation advancement through fresh reservation. Another existing generation-advancement producer, the actual adapter stop path, still leaves readonly authority and quota unresolved. This can block a retry after cancellation and reduce capacity for other Tasks; it is not absence of the planned Workflow/Registry integration.

contract_evidence.requirement: Cancellation/replacement retires both logical permissions before hygiene.
Immutable snapshot work may coexist with a fresh executor; logical fencing and bounded lease release must permit new cooperative work.

findings.proposed_control: Use one scope/epoch/generation-specific retirement helper on every executor-generation advance, including retire_execution_as and preparation/native failure paths. Atomically close the precisely affected readonly units, preserve known work and artifacts, remove their waiters, release leases and queue cleanup before changing the Task projection. Alternatively preserve explicitly authorized snapshot continuation independently of the latest executor generation. Do not grant historical-generation input/publication authority or rely on a future caller to terminalize the whole Task.
causal_controls_to_add: Account-free ledger control: published old artifact, fresh live executor E, then active reviewer/verifier from that artifact in E's generation. Retire E with cancel_task=false and assert all invalidated readonly flags and leases are closed and the next fresh attempt can reserve.

Account-free actual NativeAdapter vtable fixture: stop E while a readonly sibling is held; ensure the sibling obtains a durable conservative terminal, its lease cannot accumulate and another Task can obtain capacity.
Repeat for PreparationGuard abandonment of E and native launch/bootstrap failure paths that retire an executor with cancel_task=false.
Preserve successful prior work/retained artifacts, refuse duplicate live executors and verify foreign Task/Session/generation handles cannot stop any sibling.

Artifact/unit updates precede final Task/Workflow CAS, so a later CAS failure rolls those changes and context insertion back; in-memory Task/Record versions update only after commit (state/mod.rs:442-444,682-720).

publish_workflow_result_tx checks successful executor identity, exact active phase/Session, Ready artifact binding, all revision references, artifact marker and dependency versions, then version-CASes the artifact and closes finalization (state/execution/artifacts.rs:198-280).

Standalone ResultStore publication refuses a Workflow-owned Task, and WorkflowEngine::persist selects coordinated publication when the successful active executor Session has a managed unit; it requires exactly one retained artifact marker. No current caller bypass of that routing was found in the reviewed paths.

PhaseAttempt now persists ManagedSessionRef. Transition validation makes a bound identity immutable and limits its initial binding to native launch; the Store independently cross-checks unit scope/generation/epoch/Session binding for persisted history (workflow.rs:2406-2441; state/mod.rs:591-605).

NativeAdapter is private, and ordinary start refuses unmanaged launch. Its managed start validates provider/alias, exact input, role, project and owned worktree before NativeSessions admission. Status/stop/approvals/subscription/release require the exact in-memory managed handle and configured agent/provider identity.
NativeAdapter transport_succeeded uses saved managed work and Session identity rather than a generic exit code. Work and cleanup remain separate; no fixture establishes native cleanup guarantee.
